# 15 — Finite-Field Polynomial Algebra

This chapter treats $\mathbb F_p[x]$ the way Chapters 01–02 treat integers.  Division,
gcd, irreducibility, and factorization work because coefficients form a field.

## 1. Euclidean algebra

Normalize every nonzero gcd to monic.  Extended Euclid returns $aA+bB=\gcd(A,B)$
and gives inverses in $\mathbb F_p[x]/(M)$ exactly when the gcd is one.  Modular
polynomial exponentiation reduces after each multiplication; with fast
multiplication and remainder it is the basic engine below.

The quotient $\mathbb F_p[x]/(f)$ is a field iff $f$ is irreducible. When
$\deg f=d$, every residue class $\alpha$ in that field satisfies
$\alpha^{p^d}=\alpha$. This Frobenius structure replaces trial division over all
possible polynomial factors.

## 2. Remove multiplicities first

For $f' \ne  0$, $\gcd(f,f')$ contains repeated factors.  Separate the square-free
parts before randomized splitting.  In characteristic $p$, $f'=0$ means every
nonzero exponent is divisible by $p$; take the formal p-th root and recurse.
Missing this branch is the classic finite-field factorization bug.

## 3. Degree decomposition

The polynomial $x^{p^{d}}-x$ is the product of all monic irreducibles whose degree
divides $d$.  Repeatedly compute Frobenius powers modulo $f$ and gcds to perform
**distinct-degree factorization**.  A block is then a product of irreducibles of
one known degree.

For **equal-degree factorization**, Cantor–Zassenhaus chooses random $a(x)$ and,
for odd $p$, splits with

$$\gcd\left(f,a^{(p^{d}-1)/2}-1\right).$$

Restart when the gcd is trivial.  Over $\mathbb F_2$, use a trace-style sum rather than
the half-order exponent.  Berlekamp instead finds the nullspace of the Frobenius
map $h\mapsto h^{p}-h$; for square-free $f$, its kernel dimension is the number
of irreducible factors.

## 4. Root finding and certification

Linear factors are $\gcd(f,x^{p}-x)$.  Factor that square-free component to list
roots.  Return roots with multiplicities only after square-free decomposition.
For every randomized algorithm, the final certificate is deterministic:
multiply the monic factors, restore multiplicities, and compare with the monic
input.

## Implementation contract

- Coefficients lie in a prime field; composite coefficient moduli invalidate division.
- Keep polynomials trimmed and gcds monic.
- Polynomial modular exponentiation must reduce degrees after every multiply.
- Random splitters need independent retries and a deterministic reconstruction check.
- Complexity depends on multiplication $M(n)$; state whether a routine is naive or NTT-based.
